analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the one who appears, and אֶל אַבְרָם identifies Abram as the one to whom he appears. The verse recalls the event in הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו, “who appeared to him.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a third-person masculine singular Niphal wayyiqtol. Its subject is יַהְוֶה.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּרָא יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, Abram is the person to whom Yahweh appeared. The verse repeats this relation in הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו, “who appeared to him.”
analysis.morphology: Simple Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Marks the person to whom someone appears.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּרָא יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, Abram is the person to whom Yahweh appears. Yahweh then addresses him directly in לְזַרְעֲךָ, “to your offspring.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The preceding preposition אֶל is a separate word.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: Yahweh addresses Abram directly. In לְזַרְעֲךָ אֶתֵּן אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת, “I will give this land to your descendants,” the promised gift identifies Abram’s offspring as the recipients.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks the recipient. The masculine singular noun is collective and stands in construct with the second-person masculine singular possessive suffix ךָ, referring to Abram.
analysis.sense: Abram’s descendants as recipients of the land promise

analysis.evidence: Yahweh promises Abram, “To your offspring I will give this land.” לְזַרְעֲךָ identifies the recipient, and אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת marks “this land” as the direct object of אֶתֵּן.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, first person common singular. The initial אֶ־ marks the first person, and the dagesh in תּ reflects assimilation of the first root consonant נ.
analysis.sense: give land to someone as a possession

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת (“this land”) as the direct object of אֶתֵּן (“I will give”). לְזַרְעֲךָ (“to your offspring”) identifies the recipient.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לְזַרְעֲךָ אֶתֵּן אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת, “I will give this land to your offspring,” הַזֹּאת identifies the particular territory promised to Abram’s descendants.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes the absolute singular noun אֶרֶץ, a noun of both genders. The feminine singular demonstrative הַזֹּאת shows feminine agreement here.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ, the direct object מִזְבֵּחַ identifies what Abram built there: an altar to YHWH.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ precedes the shortened Qal wayyiqtol form יִּבֶן, third person masculine singular. Its subject is Abram.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ, “he built an altar there,” שָׁם locates Abram’s act of building at the place where Yahweh appeared to him.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew adverb of place with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ לַיַהְוֶה means “he built an altar there to Yahweh.” מִזְבֵּחַ names what Abram built, and לַיַהְוֶה identifies the one to whom he dedicated it.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular, in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse opens with וַיֵּרָא יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, “YHWH appeared to Abram.” The closing phrase הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו, “who appeared to him,” recalls that event and identifies the one to whom Abram built the altar.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ marks the Niphal masculine singular absolute participle נִּרְאֶה, which modifies the divine name.

analysis.evidence: The verse opens with וַיֵּרָא יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, “Yahweh appeared to Abram.” The closing הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו, “who appeared to him,” recalls that appearance. The suffix takes the place of Abram’s name.
